title: International Pantry Staples for Pregnancy Nutrition
excerpt: Oats, Greek yogurt, lentils, low-mercury salmon, eggs, leafy greens and citrus — practical ways to build balanced plates.
content:
## Introduction
When pregnant, choosing the right foods is crucial to ensure the health and well-being of both mother and baby. In this article, we will explore international pantry staples that are good for pregnancy, helping to build balanced and nutritious meals.

## Nutrient Analysis
The following international pantry staples are excellent choices for pregnant women:
- Oats: rich in fiber, helping to support digestive health and reduce the risk of constipation.
- Greek yogurt: rich in calcium, protein and beneficial bacteria, helping to support bone health and the immune system.
- Lentils: rich in protein, fiber and iron, helping to support the development of the fetus and reduce the risk of anemia.
- Low-mercury salmon: rich in omega-3 fatty acids, helping to support the development of the brain and eyes of the fetus.
- Eggs: rich in protein, vitamins and minerals, helping to support the development of the fetus.
- Leafy greens and citrus: rich in vitamins, minerals and fiber, helping to support overall health and reduce the risk of vitamin deficiencies.

## What to Combine and Avoid
To build balanced meals, pregnant women should combine these pantry staples with other foods such as:
- Combining oats with Greek yogurt and fruit to create a nutritious breakfast.
- Adding lentils to stews and soups to increase protein and fiber content.
- Cooking low-mercury salmon with leafy greens and citrus to create a meal rich in omega-3 fatty acids and vitamins.
- Eggs can be combined with leafy greens and citrus to create a meal rich in protein and vitamins.

## Practical Tips
To ensure food safety, pregnant women should:
- Wash hands thoroughly before preparing and eating food.
- Wash all fruits and vegetables thoroughly before eating.
- Cook food to a safe temperature to avoid food poisoning.
- Avoid eating expired or spoiled food.

## When to Seek Help
If pregnant women have any questions or concerns about nutrition or health, they should seek help from a doctor or registered dietitian. They can provide personalized advice and guidance to help pregnant women build a safe and healthy nutrition plan.
